answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly assign a small set of identities to the same task and reward only outputs that agree with independently verified results. If a cluster of Sybils coordinates a false answer, audits can expose the mismatch and slash every participating stake, so spawning identities does not multiply influence without risk. The inlet may be narrow, but a comet of fake accounts still faces the gale of capital tied up and lost.
